blog.title: Posts
blog.description: Notes on software development and things I have learned.

about.title: About
about.description: Email and GitHub for software engineer Jingeon Kim.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.description: What visit statistics this blog collects and how to turn them off.

side-project-design.title: How my side project plans and screens changed
side-project-design.description: A private photo contest became an ongoing community. I chose a first game for Game Mate and changed the home, signup, and profile screens as I tried them.

puppeteer-event-lifecycle.title: Waiting for Puppeteer requests and responses without leaking listeners
puppeteer-event-lifecycle.description: I needed to wait for both a request and its response in Puppeteer. This is how I handled event ordering, listener cleanup, and timeouts.

electron-module-boundaries.title: Separating responsibilities in an Electron data-collection app
electron-module-boundaries.description: I separated the shared workflow from platform-specific code in an Electron data-collection app. I also describe why I removed NestJS after feedback from the CTO.

query-key-factory.title: Keeping TanStack Query keys and query functions together
query-key-factory.description: I kept query keys and query functions together so callers could choose whether to invalidate a list, a detail query, or a wider cache.

typescript-patterns.title: Using TypeScript to catch mistakes at the call site
typescript-patterns.description: These are the TypeScript patterns I use to preserve inference and express relationships between values: satisfies, optional properties, generics, and mutually exclusive props.

nextjs-tanstack-query-ssr.title: Using TanStack Query with the Next.js App Router
nextjs-tanstack-query-ssr.description: I gave server requests and the browser different QueryClient lifetimes, then connected server-prefetched data to client queries.

reservation-form-state.title: Moving reservation form state from Zustand to React Hook Form
reservation-form-state.description: Adding a family member could disturb the selected reservation date. I separated server data from the draft and brought the form values into React Hook Form.

review-like-optimistic-update.title: Updating review likes in list and detail caches
review-like-optimistic-update.description: A review like appears in both list and detail caches. I updated them together and restored saved snapshots when the request failed.

nextjs-seo-prefetch.title: When to await prefetch in the Next.js App Router
nextjs-seo-prefetch.description: Data appeared in the browser but was missing from the initial HTML. I separated queries the server must await from those it can stream while pending.

review-form-funnel.title: Separating state and steps in a review form
review-form-funnel.description: I separated input values, validation, and navigation in a review flow, including how multi-selection connected to the form and the constraints that remained.

typed-program-form.title: Sharing a program form across two admin apps
typed-program-form.description: Two admin apps shared program inputs but had different submission flows. I separated field types and API transformations while deciding what to share.

cross-domain-token-handoff.title: Handing authentication between separate hosts
cross-domain-token-handoff.description: Moving settlement pages to another host required an authentication handoff. I compared URL and POST-body delivery and considered the session problems that remained.

chatbot-message-layer.title: Connecting two SSE streams to one chat interface
chatbot-message-layer.description: Answer generation and final messages arrived through separate SSE streams. I split their responsibilities to keep one coherent message flow.

sitemap-api-boundaries.title: Separating public and authenticated reads in a sitemap
sitemap-api-boundaries.description: A shared interceptor read authentication cookies inside the sitemap cache. I separated public reads from member-specific reads and chose the cache boundary.

payment-coupon-branches.title: Handling coupon branches in payment history
payment-coupon-branches.description: Adding coupons changed the data, inputs, and submission rules in payment history. I describe how I organized those branches and their state.

fsd-layer-boundaries.title: Redrawing FSD boundaries for the codebase
fsd-layer-boundaries.description: The boundary between entities and features was too vague to explain where files belonged. I used actual dependencies to redraw layers and import rules.

prototype-working-rules.title: Keeping working rules from a prototype migration
prototype-working-rules.description: While moving a prototype into a Next.js proof of concept, I recorded repeated decisions in skills and revised rules that were too broad.

testing-standards.title: The standards I developed while introducing tests
testing-standards.description: After introducing tests, I refined them against real submission paths and server constraints. I review what a test verifies as well as whether it passes.

declarative-code.title: How I write declarative code
declarative-code.description: I separate UI, data, and behavior by context and keep each section at a consistent level of abstraction. These examples reflect the standards I record in skills.

nextjs-server-client-issues.title: Tracing Next.js routing and cache problems
nextjs-server-client-issues.description: I traced searches that did not update the URL and chunk errors after an upgrade, then distinguished server navigation from URL-only state changes.

error-boundary-recovery.title: Letting failed sections recover with Error Boundaries
error-boundary-recovery.description: I split error boundaries so a failed query would not replace the whole screen, alongside response validation, error reporting, and retry behavior.

low-effort-success.title: Making the next success take less effort
low-effort-success.description: A question about success, failure, and effort made me think about another criterion: whether today's effort makes the next task easier.

sentry-observability.title: Connecting Sentry errors, Web Vitals, MCP, and releases
sentry-observability.description: I connected browser and server errors to Sentry, set reporting policies and severity levels, and verified Web Vitals, MCP access, and release artifacts.

plan-gated-ai-workflow.title: The development workflow I refined with coding agents
plan-gated-ai-workflow.description: I recorded repeated decisions in skills, lint rules, and tests while delegating implementation to coding agents. I review the plan and finished changes, then check the code and the running UI.

zod-assertion-boundaries.title: Runtime validation beyond type assertions
zod-assertion-boundaries.description: Removing type assertions led me to separate failure handling for API responses, URLs, and forms. A narrower type does not necessarily mean a safer runtime value.

bottom-sheet-drag-crash.title: Tracing a Bottom Sheet drag crash with Sentry
bottom-sheet-drag-crash.description: I traced a drag-release crash into the sheet library, preserved snap positions through an upgrade, and later addressed a header-scrolling problem I had missed.

health-check-program.title: Bringing health-check reservations into the existing service
health-check-program.description: I brought health-check reservations from an external site and phone calls into the member storefront and two admin apps, connecting program management, test selection, applications, and payment.

reading-ai-code.title: Why I still read the code
reading-ai-code.description: Black-box checks alone led to a sprint full of hotfixes. I now pair them with white-box testing that starts from reading the code, and keep the code manageable enough to read.

side-project-infrastructure.title: Starting with one EC2 instance
side-project-infrastructure.description: I dropped RDS to reduce initial cost and chose a small EC2 instance with PostgreSQL. Along the way I explored serverless and R2 and fixed S3 permissions that broke CI.

side-project-technology.title: GraphQL for the photo service, REST for Game Mate
side-project-technology.description: Why the services use different APIs and caches, how their contracts and database writes work, and how ESLint rules and fixtures check module boundaries.
